config.question: given the gaps papers report between two accuracy-like values, how large would a shared test set have to be for those gaps to be distinguishable from zero
config.why: a reviewer noted that our definition of testable assumes variance across runs, while for a fixed test set the dominant uncertainty is over examples and a binomial interval needs only the accuracy and the test-set size
config.conservatism: the two values are treated as independent binomials; two systems scored on the same items are positively correlated, so a paired test would need fewer, and the stated requirement is an upper bound

metrics.filter: both values in [40,100], the range where a metric is almost certainly an accuracy or similar rate

notes: This needs no error bars at all, only the printed means, so it covers 544 papers against the 121 that carry enough for the variance-based test. The median reported gap of 1.4 points would need a test set of about twelve thousand items; 79 percent of comparisons would need one larger than GSM8K.
